Supports value refs (dollar-brace syntax), exec refs (dollar-paren syntax), fallback defaults (:-), and required checks (:?). Backslash-escape emits literals (backslash consumed on output). Recursive with circular-ref detection. --source flag skips interpolation on get; --plain only strips colors. (--raw was a deprecated alias for --plain since v1.9.1; removed entirely in v1.11.)

SECURITY MODEL (v1.2.1, exec-on-read RCE fix): executing a dollar-paren exec ref is OPT-IN. interpolate() defaults allowExec=false and leaves dollar-paren LITERAL; only interpolateExec() runs the stored command via execSync. Reason: substitution happens on read/list/json/lint/dry/preview paths, not just run — a hostile cloned .reverie/ store could RCE the moment an agent read an entry. INVARIANT: only the actual run-execution moment (CLI runCommand past the dry/confirm gate; MCP reverie_run past dry+confirm) may call interpolateExec on RAW values. Every display/preview/dry/confirm path MUST use the safe interpolate(). dollar-brace value refs always resolve; a value that itself contains dollar-paren stays literal in safe mode (no exec via indirection). DO NOT reintroduce exec on any read path.

RUN GATE WALK (#289, #292): before a run, collectRunReferences walks its values in exec's order with exec's cache sharing — one cache per CLI run (segments and --chain included), one per member for MCP chain:true — and marks a walked dollar-paren ref as exec does, so the walk never goes deeper than exec. A walk that stops on an error after passing a command exec would run gates the run (walkUnchecked, reason in the prompt); one that stops before any command keeps its own error. Each a:b segment is interpolated in its own store. Names gated per lookup: as typed, the alias target, and the global alias target when project aliases were used (Resolution.gateNames, decided with the lookup since #305 L12). While the global _aliases.json is unreadable, a run whose first name was looked up through project aliases asks (#303.1, owner; unreadableGlobalAliasesFor, decided at the first lookup and carried to --chain members). KNOWN LIMIT, OWNER-ACCEPTED 2026-11-27 (#305 L14): the gate walks the store as it is before the run, and exec reads it again. A dollar-paren command that writes entries mid-run, or (CLI only) another session writing while the y/N prompt waits, changes what later refs read, unchecked. Accepted because a command that can write the store could run rvr run <flagged> --yes itself; documented in README Run Confirmation. Rejected: gate and run from one snapshot (the walk records each lookup, exec reads only those). Do not re-propose without a new case.
